AI Mode replied:

To get a
runny yolk
with firm whites, boil large, fridge-cold eggs in boiling water for 6 minutes. 
How to Cook the Eggs
  • Boil water first: Fill a pot with enough water to cover the eggs and bring it to a rolling boil.
  • Add the eggs: Use a spoon to gently lower cold eggs straight from the refrigerator into the boiling water.
  • Adjust heat: Lower the heat slightly to a gentle boil so the eggs do not crack against each other.
  • Set a timer: Cook for 6 minutes for a liquid, runny yolk and set whites. Cook for 5 minutes if you want an extra runny center, or 7 minutes if you prefer a thicker, jammy consistency
    .
     
Cooling and Peeling
  • Use an ice bath: Prepare a bowl of cold water and ice cubes before you start. 
  • Stop the cooking: Immediately transfer the hot eggs into the ice bath using a slotted spoon and let them sit for at least 3 to 5 minutes. 
  • Peel gently: Tap the cooled egg on a hard surface to crack the shell, then peel it gently, preferably under cold running water to help release the shell. 
If you'd like, let me know:
  • Are you using large, medium, or jumbo eggs?
  • Are the eggs straight from the fridge or at room temperature?
I can help you fine-tune the exact timer for your specific setup.
